div.ab: LXXXVIIII. Burgbryce mon sceal betan CXX scill. kyninges ⁊ biscepes, þær his rice bið; ealdormonnes LXXX scill.; cyninges ðegnes LX scill.; gesiðcundes monnes landhæbbendes XXXV; ⁊ bi ðon ansacan.
LXXXIX. Burhbryce mon scel betan mid CXX scll' cyninges ⁊ biscopes, ðær his rice bið; ealdormonnes LXXX scll'; cyninges ðegnes LX scll'; gesiðcundes monnes londhæbbendes XXXV scll'; ⁊ by þon onsacan.

Be burhbryce. Burhbryce man sceal betan hundtwelftig scill' cyninges ⁊ bisceopes, ðær his rice bið; ealdormannes hundeahtatig scill'; cyninges ðegnas syxti scill'; gesiðcundes mannes landhæbbendes fif ⁊ XXX scill' ⁊ bi ð[am] onsacan.

Burchbreche (burgi fractura) debet emendari centum uiginti solid. regis et episcopi, ubi suum riche (id est sedes eius) est; aldermanni LXXX solid.; þegnes (thaini) regis LX sol.; et gesiðcundes (siþcundi) hominis terram habentis XXXV sol.; aut per id negare.

[Be Burhbryce.] Burgbryce mon sceal betan CXX scill. kyninges ⁊ biscepes, þær his rice bið; ealdormonnes LXXX scill.; cyninges ðegnes LX scill.; gesiðcundes monnes landhæbbendes XXXV [scll']; ⁊ bi ðon ansacan.
{LXXXVIIII} Burgbryce mon sceal betan CXX sciƚƚ kyninges ⁊ biscepes, þær his rice bið; ealdormonnes LXXX sciƚƚ; cyninges ðegnes LX sciƚƚ; gesiðcundes monnes landhæbbendas XXXV; ⁊ bi ðon ansacan.

Burg- [oder Haus]einbruch soll man mit 120 Schill. büssen [beim Hause] des Königs und Bischofs, so weit des letzteren Diöcese reicht, [bei dem] eines Ealdorman mit 80 Schill., eines Königsthegn mit 60 Schill., eines grundbesitzenden Mannes vom Gefolgschaftsstande mit 35 (Schill.), und gemäss diesem [Werthe von jener Missethat] sich frei schwören.

Breaking into a fortified dwelling [or house] is to be compensated with 120 shillings [in the case of the house] of the king and of the bishop, as far as the latter’s diocese extends; [in the case of that] of an ealdorman with 80 shillings, of a king’s thegn with 60 shillings, of a landholding man of the retainer class with 35 (shillings); and [one may] swear oneself free [of that offence] according to this [value].

120 shillings compensation shall be paid for breaking into the fortified premises of the king or [those of] a bishop within his sphere of jurisdiction; [for breaking into those] of an ealdorman 80 shillings; into those of a king's thegn 60 shillings; into those of a nobleman who holds land 35 shillings. The accusation may be denied by oaths corresponding to these amounts.

Forcible entry into the residence of the king or the bishop, within his own diocese, one shall compensate with 120 shillings; [into that] of an ealdorman, with 80 shillings; [into that] of a king’s thegn, with 60 shillings; [into that] of a gesith-born man who owns land, with 35 shillings; and deny it correspondingly.

Breaking into a fortified dwelling shall be recompensed [at the rate of] 120 shillings for king or bishop within his realm; 80 shillings for an ealdorman; 60 shillings for a king’s thegn; 35 shillings for a landowner of noble rank; and these same amounts serve [as the value of] the oath of denial.

Vgl. Gl Einbruch 2d; Haus 1. a. Die für diesen Schutzbruch dem König zufallende Summe ist zwar die des ‘Ungehorsams’ (s. d. Gl) gegen ihn; die übrigen Summen dagegen decken sich nicht mit den Busszahlen für Schutzbruch der anderen Dynasten

Cf. Gl Einbruch 2d; Haus 1. a. The sum falling to the king for this breach of protection is indeed that for ‘disobedience’ (see that word in Gl) towards him; the other sums, on the other hand, do not coincide with the amounts of compensation for breach of the protection of the other magnates

S. Gl Bischof 13e; nicht auf Gütern, die ihm oder seiner Kathedrale ausserhalb des Amtsprengels gehören; vgl. Toller biscoprice: dioecesis; und Ann. Agsax. zu 1006: B. feng to þam rice. Es beweist dies, dass Ine nicht bloss Eine Diözese beherrschte; s. o. Pro.¹⁰

See Gl Bischof 13e; not on estates belonging to him or his cathedral outside his official district; cf. Toller biscoprice: dioecesis; and Ann. Agsax. under 1006: B. feng to þam rice. This proves that Ine did not rule over a single diocese only; see above Pro.¹⁰

Lit. ‘breaking through the fortifications of,’ etc. It would seem that the residences of the higher classes were usually surrounded by some kind of stockade. Stones or earth can hardly have been used; otherwise such residences would frequently be traceable now.
i.e. within his diocese.

From a comparison of this law with Alf. cap. 40, it seems probable, that in spite of the slight difference in the amount stated, the phrase gesiðcundes monnes landhæbbendes is equivalent to the more usual twelfhynde man; though this identification is not allowed by Liebermann.
